In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
whistler waves are attenuated by 10 dB in the day and 20 dB in night, and that the lower hybrid waves propagate to the magnetosphere and are observed by satellites.
the attenuation of VLF waves in the presence short-scale striations in Earth’s lower ionosphere can account most of the ∼20 dB observed loss in VLF wave intensity.
whistler mode attenuation is a result of the combined effects of mode conversion to the lower hybrid mode and scattering of the whistler mode by striations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the conversion of whistlers to lower hybrid waves is the most likely mechanism for the observed loss of intensity in whistler signals in the 20–30 kHz frequency range.
the mode conversion between whistlers and lower hybrid waves in Earth's ionospheric D region can account for most, or all, of the attenuation of whister waves observed in the magnetosphere.
the attenuation of VLF/ELV waves by the ionosphere is not a uniform process and is dependent on the wave frequency, the density striation size, the density profile and the wave polarization.
The main takeaway from our work is that
VLF waves can be attenuated by the ionosphere, even if the ionosphere is not in the lossy mode.
the ionosphere is not a transparent medium to VLF waves, and the ionosphere is a key component in the VLF wave propagation from the Earth to the magnetosphere.
the attenuation of VLF/ELFs waves by the ionosphere should be taken into account when interpreting VLF wavefield data from the magnetosphere.
